Section Score

FMS.21 — The hospital has an effective fire alarm system
FMS 21.1
Fire Alarm Inspection Schedule & Reports
Document EvidenceObservation
📋 Surveyor checks: Inspection schedule exists · Checklist includes zones/devices · Technician name & signature · Comments resolved · Linked to FMS 21.3 (score cannot exceed 21.3)
FMS 21.2
Fire Alarm Testing Schedule & Reports
Document Evidence
📋 Surveyor checks: Weekly/monthly testing records · Testing checklist per zone · Technician signed · Linked to FMS 21.3
FMS 21.3
Fire Alarm Preventive Maintenance (Certified Contractor)
Document Evidence
⚠️ CRITICAL: PPM must be by Civil Defense certified company — hospital staff cannot score this. This standard gates FMS 21.1 and 21.2.
FMS 21.4
Fire Alarm Connected to Elevators
Document ReviewObservation
📋 Surveyor will: Check fire alarm distribution drawing showing elevator connection · Test one elevator to confirm it returns to ground floor on alarm activation
FMS.22 — The hospital has a fire suppression system available in required areas
FMS 22.1
Sprinkler System — Inspection, PPM & Fire Pump
ObservationDocument Evidence
📋 Surveyor will visit fire pump room: jockey/electrical/diesel pumps on AUTO · Sprinkler heads not obstructed/painted · Spacing ≤5m in ordinary risk · Quarterly PPM must be by Civil Defense certified company
FMS 22.2
Clean Agent Suppression System (Server Rooms, Electrical, Generators)
ObservationDocument Evidence
📋 Required locations: Medical records · Server/Data center · Electrical rooms · Generator rooms. Inspection tag must be current. CO2 acceptable in unoccupied areas only.
FMS 22.3
Wet Chemical System — Kitchen Hood
ObservationDocument Evidence
📋 Surveyor will visit kitchen · Check inspection tag is current · Ensure function not blocked by adjacent installations · Quarterly PPM by Civil Defense certified company required
FMS 22.4
Stand Pipes & Hose Reel System
ObservationDocument Evidence
📋 Surveyor will physically check at least one hose reel pressure (automatic activation) · Ensure no adjacent installations blocking stand pipes · Quarterly PPM by Civil Defense certified company

Safety Manager — Moe
FMS 23.1–24.5 · Fire Exits, Evacuation & Fire Safety
Section Score
—
FMS.23 — The hospital ensures safe fire exits and evacuation routes
FMS 23.1
Fire Exits — Availability & Location
Observation
⚠️ CRITICAL GATE: Score of FMS 23.1 limits FMS 23.2, 23.3, 23.4, 23.6 — none can score higher than this. Not mandatory to have 2 exits per room — depends on occupants, travel distance, area type (refer to SBC).
FMS 23.2
Fire Exits — Not Locked
Observation
📋 Surveyor will TEST 3–5 fire exits. If access control/keys used → must have key boxes, manual press buttons, and clear signage. Score cannot exceed FMS 23.1.
FMS 23.3
Fire Exits — No Obstructions (Both Ends)
Observation
📋 Surveyor checks BOTH ends of exit route (inside and outside). Common failures: furniture, project debris, cardboard boxes. Score cannot exceed FMS 23.1.
FMS 23.4
Fire Exits — Panic Hardware (Direction of Evacuation)
Observation
📋 Exit doors must open in the direction of evacuation (outward) with panic/crash bar hardware. Score cannot exceed FMS 23.1.
FMS 23.6
Fire Exits — Illuminated Exit Signs
Observation
📋 All fire exits must have illuminated (lit) exit signs. Non-illuminated or missing signs = Not Met. Score cannot exceed FMS 23.1.
FMS.24 — The hospital and its occupants are safe from fire and smoke
FMS 24.1
No-Smoking Policy
Document ReviewObservation
📋 Policy must cover: cigarettes, e-cigarettes, pipe, water pipe, incense. Must include disciplinary actions. Surveyor will check roof, mechanical rooms, entrances for cigarette butts.
FMS 24.2
Access to Fire Extinguishers, Alarm Boxes & Fire Blankets
Observation
📋 No obstructions to fire extinguishers, alarm boxes, or fire blankets. Surveyor checks during building tour.
FMS 24.3
Emergency Evacuation Lighting
Observation
📋 Surveyor will FUNCTIONALLY TEST emergency lights (cut power / press test button). Battery backup mandatory in OR and generator room only. Must be adequate for safe evacuation.
FMS 24.4
Storage Areas — Safe & Organized (incl. Central Supply)
Observation
⚠️ Pay special attention to CENTRAL SUPPLY STORE. Surveyor will: test emergency doors, check exit signage, inspect fire extinguishers, verify access control, assess safe storage protocol.
FMS 24.5
Fire Rated Doors & No Fire Wall Penetrations
Observation
⚠️ CRITICAL: Surveyor will REMOVE CEILING TILES in 3 different locations to check fire wall integrity. Fire rated doors must be per hospital zones with no gaps to ceiling. Penetrations between zones = Not Met.

Biomedical Engineering — Bashar & Robert
FMS 32.1–32.12 · Medical Gas System
Section Score
—
FMS.32 — The hospital ensures proper maintenance of the medical gas system
FMS 32.1
PMG Preventive Maintenance Schedule & Reports
Document Evidence
📋 Must cover ALL PMG components: manifolds, air compressor, liquid oxygen (LOX), and suction system. Schedule and completed maintenance reports required.
FMS 32.2
Medical Gas Policy & Procedures
Document Review
📋 Policy must include ALL 4 elements: 1) Taking system offline 2) Modifying/testing PMG 3) Ordering/refilling LOX 4) Documenting repairs/alterations/tests/filling logs/consumption
FMS 32.3
Compressed Medical Air — Purity Testing (with Exact Values)
Document Evidence
⚠️ CRITICAL: Test report must include EXACT measured values vs limits — Humidity/Dewpoint ≤-46°C · CO ≤5ppm · CO₂ ≤500ppm · SO₂ ≤1ppm · Water ≤0.05mg/L · Particles
FMS 32.4
Medical Gas Rooms — Safe & Secure
Observation
📋 Surveyor will physically inspect manifold room + compressor room: locked · proper signage · clean · no oil · no exposed wiring. Applicable to ALL hospitals including those using only cylinders.
FMS 32.5
PMG Outlets — Functioning, Unified Label & Connection Type
Observation
📋 Each gas type must have same label and same connector type throughout hospital. Mix of connector types for same gas = Not Met (patient safety risk).
FMS 32.6
Medical Gas Pipes — Clearly Identified (Type & Direction per SBC)
Observation
📋 Pipes must be color-coded and labeled with gas type and flow direction as per Saudi Building Code (SBC). Surveyor checks accessible pipe runs.
FMS 32.8
O₂ Standby Supply — 48-Hour Sufficiency & No Active Alarms
ObservationStaff Interview
⚠️ Surveyor will INTERVIEW utility manager on daily O₂/air consumption rate. Will check no active alarms at manifold. Formula: 1L LOX ≈ 855L gas @20°C · 1 K-cylinder ≈ 6800L @2000psi
FMS 32.9
Gas Cylinders — Regularly Tested (Type, Amount, Leaks)
Observation
📋 Surveyor observes cylinder testing records and may physically check cylinders for labeling, amount gauge, and leak detection.
FMS 32.10
Valve Box Labels & Staff Awareness of PMG Shutoff Valves
ObservationStaff Interview
📋 Surveyor will INTERVIEW clinical staff: Do they know shutoff valve locations? Can they demonstrate how to close safely? Labels must show room numbers served by each valve box.
FMS 32.11
Valve Shutoff Responsible Staff — Risk Awareness
Staff Interview
📋 Specifically the staff RESPONSIBLE for valve shutoff must know: 1) Risk associated with shutting off valves 2) Risk of breaking valve box cover 3) Which rooms/areas are affected by closing each valve
FMS 32.12
PMG Outlets — Adequate in Patient Care Areas & Error-Proof
Observation
📋 Outlets must be adequate in number for patient care needs AND error-proof (DISS/NIST fittings — each gas connector physically incompatible with other gases, preventing wrong gas connection).

Connecting to Google Sheets...
Apps Script URL:
📋 Two-step setup to connect your Google Sheet
Step 1 — Make sheet public (if not done)
1. Open your Google Sheet
2. Click Share (top right)
3. Click Change to anyone with the link
4. Set permission to Viewer
5. Click Done
Step 2 — Deploy Apps Script (solves CORS)
1. In your Sheet: Extensions → Apps Script
2. Paste the script shown below → Save
3. Click Deploy → New deployment → Web App
4. Set Execute as: Me · Anyone can access
5. Copy the URL, paste below, click Connect
function doGet(e) { var ss = SpreadsheetApp.openById('10qPGTtY0k9cBNAeYEwyKwpebsYMndvEFkhFB0RRO0q8'); var sheet = ss.getSheets().find(s => s.getSheetId() == 1530231215) || ss.getSheets()[0]; var data = sheet.getDataRange().getValues(); var headers = data[0]; var rows = data.slice(1) .filter(function(r){ return r[0] || r[11]; }) .map(function(r){ return r.map(String); }); return ContentService .createTextOutput(JSON.stringify({headers: headers.map(String), rows: rows})) .setMimeType(ContentService.MimeType.JSON); }

🎓 Staff PMG Competency Assessment — Annex I
COMPETENCY ITEMS — Mark each as Competent (C) / Needs Improvement (NI) / Not Applicable (N/A)
For ALL Staff:
Knows the location of the ZSV serving their work area and which rooms it serves
Can identify the correct gas outlet color coding (O₂ white, Air yellow, Suction black)
Knows who to call for gas failure (Biomedical ext. 6130) and what to do immediately
Understands no combustibles/ignition sources near O₂ outlets
Can demonstrate connecting and disconnecting from an O₂ terminal outlet safely
For Biomedical Engineers only:
Can perform LOX daily gauge reading and calculate reserve hours correctly
Can execute the planned ZSV offline procedure including two-person rule and portable O₂ deployment
Knows the CBAHI medical air purity limits (CO ≤5ppm, CO₂ ≤500ppm, SO₂ ≤1ppm, Dewpoint ≤-46°C)
